solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Filthy place where cops lose criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters of the words that follow are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A grimy den where the police shed lawbreakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun the cops are losing, but it signals the anagram of COPS LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspool is a pit for sewage, so it is literally a filthy place, and figuratively any den of corruption.

clue.text: Company not out to make money

parts.note: a batsman who is not out is still in, in cricket

explanation.surface: A business that stays in play in order to earn.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman 'not out' is still IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin is to mint new currency, the literal way of producing money.

clue.text: Means of crossing forest location between streets, working east

indicators.note: between tells us the forest's name sits in the middle of the two street abbreviations

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, and two streets give it twice
Epping Forest is an ancient woodland on the edge of London, and Epping is the town it is named for
a machine that is working is on
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Directions for finding a path through woodland between roads, heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: EPPING is a town on the edge of London beside Epping Forest; it sits between two STs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone is a flat rock placed in a stream to let walkers cross it.

clue.text: Shake oil paint apt to run

indicators.note: paint that runs drips out of shape, so these letters are set flowing into a new order

explanation.surface: Stir the oil paint so it will flow properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to run' is the anagram signal on OIL PAINT APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A palpitation is a fluttering or trembling, especially of the heart, so it is a shake in noun form.

clue.text: Revealed non-professional expenditure

parts.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
lay describes people without professional or clerical training

explanation.surface: An amateur's spending has come to light.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money laid out, an amount spent on something.

clue.text: Caught pub returning seafood

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: returning means the word for the pub is read backwards

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone caught heading back to the pub for a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab is a shellfish commonly eaten, one example of seafood.

clue.text: An errant merge gone wrong could lead to this?

definitions.text: An errant merge gone wrong could lead to this?

indicators.note: a merge gone wrong leaves its parts out of order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A botched merger might leave things reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone wrong' signals the anagram of AN ERRANT MERGE, and the whole clue describes the result: jumbling those letters is itself a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement is a changed order, exactly what scrambling the letters of a phrase produces.

clue.text: Rubbish round Madrid arena

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense or rubbish
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: Nonsense spoken about a Spanish stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid has a famous bullring, Las Ventas, an arena where bullfights are staged; Madrid makes it an example.

clue.text: Perfect one to buy and sell

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to deal is to trade, buying and selling goods

explanation.surface: A flawless item to trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, matching an imagined standard.

clue.text: Little piggy's end not a lie, tragically

indicators.note: something gone tragically has gone badly awry, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A sad truth about the fate of the little pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This little piggy' is the nursery rhyme counted on a child's toes, so a little piggy is a toe; its end is the nail. 'tragically' signals the anagram of NOT A LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme each little piggy is a toe, and the nail sits at the toe's tip.

clue.text: Searingly? Wearingly? They both do this delightfully

definitions.text: Searingly? Wearingly? They both do this
definitions.meaning: both quoted words finish with the same eight letters, so read the answer as a phrase saying what they do: end in that string

explanation.surface: Two adverbs share a charming trait.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as END EARINGLY: that is what both SEARINGLY and WEARINGLY do.
explanation.definitionFit: Endearingly means in a way that wins affection, so charmingly or delightfully.

clue.text: Wolf upset plain herder

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A wolf disturbs a simple shepherd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolf' paints a predator troubling a herdsman, but it is a womaniser here; 'upset' signals the anagram of PLAIN HERDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf is slang for a man who chases women, which is what a philanderer does.

clue.text: Stress English politician has income support initially

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of each of the next two words is used

explanation.surface: An English politician on welfare is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Income Support was a UK welfare benefit, which shapes the surface; here only its first letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress or weight given to a word or idea.

clue.text: Marks yearbook carving out name by hand

parts.note: M stands for marks, the old German currency

indicators.note: carving out means a letter is cut away from the yearbook

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year

explanation.surface: Grading a school yearbook while hand-carving a name in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carving out' takes N from ANNUAL to leave ANUAL; M is for marks, the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual describes work done with the hands rather than by machine.

clue.text: Shot from gun

definitions.meaning: in billiards a ... is a shot in which the cue ball strikes two balls in turn

explanation.surface: A bullet fired from a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot from gun' reads as a single idea, but it is two definitions joined by 'from'; the shot is the billiards one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannon names both a heavy artillery gun and a billiards stroke hitting two balls.

clue.text: Girl's a new doctor in South Africa

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces sit inside the abbreviation for the country

explanation.surface: A young woman is a newly qualified doctor in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a female first name, so one example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Admit Ophelia sits awkwardly

indicators.note: sitting awkwardly means out of position, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ophelia, from Hamlet, sits uncomfortably and confesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' looks like confess, but in the hospital sense, to take in a patient; 'awkwardly' signals the anagram of OPHELIA SITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital admits a patient when it takes them in for treatment, the same as hospitalising them.

clue.text: Where horses are beginning some training under direction

indicators.note: beginning asks for the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A stable where horses start their schooling under supervision.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a farm where horses are kept for breeding.

clue.text: Behaved amourously — when papa's wife fainted

indicators.note: when papa's wife reads as 'when P is replaced by W', a letter swap

parts.note: to spoon is an old word for kissing and cuddling
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mother passed out when father got romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when papa's wife' means change P to W: SPOONED becomes the answer. Spoon is dated slang for canoodle.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, especially from strong emotion.

clue.text: Man found around western part of Wales

indicators.note: around tells us the word for a man wraps round the compass letter

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A man discovered somewhere in west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwent is a historic county in south-east Wales, so a region within the country.

clue.text: Half completed building

indicators.note: half means only the back four of the eight letters are kept

parts.note: something completed is finished

explanation.surface: A building project left only half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completed' is FINISHED; its second half is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a simple outbuilding, so a modest example of a building.

clue.text: A little scary — a tidy figure going to support building, perhaps

definitions.text: figure going to support building, perhaps

indicators.note: a little of the words means just a part of them, a run of letters inside

explanation.surface: A slightly frightening yet neat statue holding up a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' signals a run of letters inside 'scary a tidy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A caryatid is a carved female figure used as a column to hold up part of a building.
